item.title: Hybrid nanophotonic trap boosts atomic storage and coherence times
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02005-y A hybrid nanophotonic trap that replaces the attractive red-detuned laser field with atom–surface interactions — Casimir–Polder interactions and electrostatic attraction — achieves record-long storage and coherence times for cold atoms coupled to a nanofibre surface.

item.description: arXiv:2610.02821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverse design has been transformative in nanophotonics, providing an automated means of realizing high-performance, non-intuitive devices. item.description: arXiv:2610.03521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precise and programmable control of optical polarization provides a versatile vectorial degree of freedom for light-matter interaction and optical information encoding. Existing polarization state generators (PSGs), however, suffer from poor switchability and modest fidelity at the micrometer scale, which severely constrains their practical applicability. item.title: Stimulated Parametric Down-Conversion: From Foundational Coherence to Structured Light Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.03241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stimulated parametric down-conversion (StimPDC) is the seeded version of the process that underlies much of photonic quantum information. Replacing the vacuum at one input port with a coherent seed leaves the interaction Hamiltonian, the phase-matching function and the two-photon amplitude unchanged, while raising the output to levels accessible with ordinary classical detectors. This review treats the transverse spatial physics of that process.

item.description: By superimposing two ultrashort laser pulses that converge from different directions, a team of physicists at the University of Oldenburg has succeeded in generating three-dimensional light fields.

item.title: SHINE lights up the extremes
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02017-8 The Shanghai High Repetition Rate XFEL and Extreme Light Facility is approaching its first lasing. Nature Photonics spoke with Zhentang Zhao, director of the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility and the SHINE project, about the facility’s capabilities and future plans.

item.title: Time-stretch spectroscopy breaks temporal aliasing barrier
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02006-x A temporally super-resolved single-shot method overcomes the long-standing temporal–spectral trade-off in time-stretch spectroscopy. The outcome is continuous measurements of non-repetitive spectral dynamics with picosecond resolution, providing a three-orders-of-magnitude improvement over the current state of the art.

item.title: Optomechanics for piconewton force metrology
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02011-0 Of the sensors that can directly sense forces in the pico- and sub-pico-newton ranges, only a few can measure in liquids. Microfibre-based microcantilevers now add to this family, providing a versatile, broad-bandwidth, high-sensitivity optomechanical sensor.
